# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 40 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_040_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Part 2 — On Double-Mindedness

**40:1** "Lord," I said, "I wish to ask you one more thing." "Speak," he said. "Lord," I said, "I hear from certain teachers that there is no repentance beyond that which we received when we went down into the water and received forgiveness of the sins which we had previously committed."

**40:2** He said to me: "You have heard correctly, for so it is. For one who has received forgiveness of sins ought never to sin again but to dwell in purity. But since you inquire precisely about all things, I will show you this also, in order to give no excuse to those who will believe or to those who have already believed in the Lord. For those who have already believed or will believe hereafter have no repentance of sins, but they have forgiveness of the sins they previously committed."

**40:3** "For the ones who were called before these days, the Lord appointed repentance. For the Lord, knowing the heart and foreknowing all things, knew the weakness of men and the many wiles of the devil, that he would do evil to the servants of God and work wickedness against them. Therefore, being merciful, the Lord had compassion on his creation and established this repentance, and to me was given authority over this repentance."

**40:4** "But I tell you," he said, "if after that great and solemn calling anyone, being tempted by the devil, should sin, he has one repentance. But if he should sin and repent frequently, it is of no benefit for such a man; for hardly shall he live."

**40:5** I said to him: "I have come to life in hearing these things from you so precisely. For I know that if I no more add to my sins, I shall be saved." "You shall be saved," he said, "you and all who do these things."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the paratactic dialogue style of Hermas.*
